title: Renewal Discount Cap on a Contract Signed Under the Old Ceiling
scenario_text:
Aquila Systems governs renewal pricing in its Renewal Discount Policy.

Version 1 (effective 2023-01-01): "Renewal discounts of up to 25% off list are permitted."

Version 2 (effective 2025-01-01): "Renewal discounts are capped at 12% off list." v2 includes a transition clause: "A contract signed under v1 retains its negotiated discount for the remainder of its original term. Any renewal executed on or after January 1, 2025 is subject to the v2 12% renewal-discount cap, regardless of the discount on the expiring contract. Mid-term amendments that do not extend the term retain the original discount."

The CRM shows customer Meadowlark Insurance: original contract C-4120, Signed 2023-02-01, 2-year term (through 2025-01-31), Negotiated discount 22% off list. A renewal quote is being prepared, with the renewal order form scheduled for execution on 2025-01-20; the customer is insisting on keeping 22% off list.

A deal desk analyst posts in #renewals on 2025-01-13: "Meadowlark's renewal is set to sign January 20. They had 22% on the original and want to keep it. What's the maximum renewal discount I can put on the order form without an out-of-policy exception?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the CRM record, determine the maximum renewal discount permitted on Meadowlark's renewal without an exception.
question: What is the maximum renewal discount permitted on Meadowlark's renewal without an out-of-policy exception?
choices: 12% off list under v2, because the renewal is being executed 2025-01-20 (on or after January 1, 2025); the expiring contract's 22% does not carry into the renewal.
22% off list, because the original contract was signed 2023-02-01 under v1's 25% cap and that discount carries into the renewal.
25% off list, because v1 governs the customer relationship established in 2023.
Up to 25% off list, because v2's 12% cap applies only to brand-new logos, not to renewals.
